back.english: The file isn't encrypted. Its “Made private” and “Made public” rows show that those payments went to your private balance or came out of it.
Pays a Seedelf, from your public account in plain view.
Pays a Seedelf, from the one-time account of this private session in plain view.
Its metadata isn't the metadata its body commits to: what reaches the chain may be different.
Pays under a register that's already on the chain, so anyone can see whose Seedelf it goes to.
Pays a Seedelf with a reference script: Seedelf Wallet can't spend it yet.
Someone else, or another device, put these boxes under your Seedelf key: mixing them from your private balance would link the mix to whoever did it. Pay from my private balance anyway takes them.

Anyone can see that a payment from the Seedelf contract started a pool. Whoever paid you the money it uses can know it was yours, and the money you made private yourself can be traced back to your public account.

Anyone can see that a payment from the Seedelf contract started this pool, and the private UTxOs it spends end up linked to that start. Whoever paid them to you can know it was yours, and the money you made private yourself can be traced back to your public account. The change goes back to a new private UTxO.
A box that comes back from this pool can't pay a part of itself without other money: at today's fees, that requires {{least}} ₳ per box.
A box that comes back from this pool can't pay a part of itself without other money.
Someone else, or another device, put some of these boxes under your Seedelf key: mixing them links this mix, and the private UTxOs it spends, to whoever did it.
Someone else, or another device, put some boxes under your Seedelf key. Mix my boxes again leaves them out, and they never come back on their own.
Someone else, or another device, put {{count}} boxes under your Seedelf key. Mix my boxes again leaves them out, and they never come back on their own.
Someone else, or another device, put one box under your Seedelf key. Mix my boxes again leaves it out, and it never comes back on its own.
Someone else, or another device, put {{count}} boxes under your Seedelf key. Mix my boxes again leaves them out, and they never come back on their own.
Only the boxes back from Lovejoin and the money other people paid you keep the Seedelf separate from your public account. The money you made private yourself can be traced back to it.
This Seedelf is yours: the payment goes to your private balance.
Recipient {{number}}'s Seedelf is yours: that payment goes to your private balance.
That's a script's address. This payment carries no datum: some scripts will never be able to spend it, and others let anyone take it.
Recipient {{number}} is a script's address. That payment carries no datum: some scripts will never be able to spend it, and others let anyone take it.
Seedelf Wallet can't show “{{character}}” in a label. Use plain letters (no accents or ñ), digits, spaces and plain punctuation.
It isn't on the wallet's list, and anyone can copy a known token's name, so check the ID of any you swap for.
It isn't on the wallet's list or on Minswap's verified list, and anyone can copy a known token's name, so check the ID of any you swap for.
Above {{percent}}, someone who trades just before your swap can leave you close to its minimum.
{{token}} isn't on the wallet's list, and Minswap doesn't verify its ID. Anyone can copy a known token's name, so check the ID before swapping for it.
Swap for it anyway
It's yours, but Seedelf Wallet can't spend it yet
This DRep has given itself the name of one of the wallet's own options. Your voting power goes to this DRep, not to that option.
. Up to {{max}} plain characters, without accents, so that Seedelf Wallet shows the label exactly as you type it.

It adds nothing to web pages unless you turn on site connection. Then it only adds the standard Cardano wallet entry (window.cardano) to https pages and to those served from this same device (localhost, 127.0.0.1), so any of those pages can see that you use Seedelf Wallet, as with any Cardano wallet, and the wallet asks you before anything is signed.

verdicts.why: Same meaning: the file isn't encrypted, and its rows show payments went to or came from the private balance. The quoted row names match activity.title.madePrivate and madePublic (“Hecho privado”, “Hecho público”), with the glossary's “ ” quotes.
Pays a Seedelf from the public account, publicly. "a la vista" is the house rendering of "in the open" (tx.privacy.metadataHint), and the back-translation reads it adverbially, as the English means.

Same meaning: pays a Seedelf from this private session's one-time account, in the open. "a la vista" sits where the English puts "in the open", and the back-translation reads it as qualifying the payment.

Same meaning: the metadata isn't what the body commits to, and what reaches the chain can differ. The phrasing matches its Transaction details twin, tx.warn.metadataHash ("no son a los que se compromete").
Same meaning: it pays under a register already on chain, so anyone can see whose Seedelf it goes to. "registro" is the house term for register (dappUi.warn.deadRegister, tx.out.underRegister).
Same meaning, including "yet" (aún): it pays a Seedelf with a reference script that Seedelf Wallet can't spend yet.

All clauses are kept: someone else or another device put the boxes under the key, and mixing from the private balance would (conditional) tie the mix to whoever did it. The button name matches lovejoin.payPrivateAnyway ("Pagar desde mi saldo privado de todos modos").

Who learns what is unchanged. Anyone sees that money from the Seedelf contract started a pool, the payer can tell it was yours, and self-made-private money leads back to the public account ("puede rastrearse hasta"). "un pago desde el contrato" for "a spend from the contract" names the same visible fact.

All four statements are kept: the start is visible, the private UTxOs it spends are tied to it, whoever paid them can tell it was yours, and self-made-private money leads back. The change goes to a new private UTxO (glossary: el cambio).

Same meaning and amount: a box can't pay part of itself without other money, and at today's fees that takes {{least}} ₳ per box. The placeholder is kept. Both EN and ES have a plain space, not the glossary's U+00A0, before ₳ here. That comes from the English source, not the translation.
Same meaning: a box back from this pool can't pay out part of itself without other money.
Same meaning: "some of these boxes" is kept, and the mixing ties this mix and the private UTxOs it spends to whoever did it.
Same meaning: Mix my boxes again (matching lovejoin.again) leaves them out, and they never come back by themselves ("nunca vuelven por sí solas").
Compared with English _other: same meaning, {{count}} is kept, and the button name matches. It leaves them out, and they never come back by themselves.
Same meaning in the singular: one box, left out by Mix my boxes again, never comes back by itself. Neither EN nor ES has a {{count}} placeholder.
Same meaning: {{count}} boxes, left out by Mix my boxes again, never come back by themselves.

"Only" is kept (Solo): only boxes back from Lovejoin and money others paid you keep the Seedelf apart from the public account. Self-made-private money leads back to it ("hasta ella" = the public account).
Same meaning: the Seedelf is yours and the payment goes to your private balance.
Same meaning with {{number}} kept: recipient N's Seedelf is yours, and that payment goes to your private balance.
Same meaning: a script address, a payment with no datum, some scripts can never spend it (nunca podrán) and others let anyone take it.
Same meaning with {{number}} kept: no datum, some scripts can never spend it, and others let anyone take it.

Same rule with {{character}} kept. "sin acentos ni ñ" and "puntuación simple" only spell out for a Spanish reader what the rule refuses. src/shared/label.ts allows printable ASCII only, so ñ, ¿ and ¡ are refused. They narrow nothing the code allows.

Same warning: not on the wallet's list, names can be copied, so check the ID of any token you swap into ("intercambiar por" = the token received). Grammar only: "No está" is singular, but the note heads a list that can hold several tokens and the English is number-neutral. This doesn't change the meaning.
Same meaning: on neither the wallet's list nor Minswap's verified list (ni), so check the ID. It has the same singular "No está" as notListed, which is grammar only.
Same meaning: above {{percent}} (which formatPercent gives with its own %), someone trading just before your swap can leave you near its minimum.
Same meaning with {{token}} kept: not on the wallet's list, Minswap doesn't verify its ID, so check the ID before swapping into it.
Same meaning, "anyway" included. sess.unverified names this switch the same way ("activa Intercambiar por él de todos modos").
Same meaning, "yet" kept (aún). "Es tuyo" matches every sibling tx.yours.* tag.
Same meaning: the DRep took the name of one of the wallet's own options, and voting power goes to this DRep, not that option.

Same rule with {{max}} and the leading ". " kept: up to max plain characters, no accents, so the tag shows as typed. It's a literal match. shared.label.warn.badCharacter also says "ni ñ", which this hint could add for consistency, but that isn't a meaning error.

Same meaning. It adds nothing unless connecting sites is on ("la conexión de sitios", as dapp.connectorOff), then only the standard entry to https and localhost pages, so those pages can see you use Seedelf Wallet, and it asks before signing. "este mismo dispositivo" for "this computer" is the same machine. The value matches docs/store/README.md line 164.

back.english: This file is not encrypted. The "Made private" and "Made public" rows show that the payment went into the private balance, or came out of it.
Pays to a Seedelf. It goes out openly from the public account.
Pays to a Seedelf. It goes out openly from this private session's disposable account.
The metadata doesn't match what the body commits to. What goes on chain may differ from what is shown.
Because it pays with a register that's already on chain, anyone can check whose Seedelf it goes into.
Pays to a Seedelf with a reference script attached. Seedelf Wallet can't use this yet.

These boxes were put in, addressed to your Seedelf key, by another person or another device. If you mix from the private balance, that mix is tied to the person who put them in. "Pay from the private balance anyway" handles them too.

Anyone can tell that the pool was started by a payment from the Seedelf contract. Whoever paid you the money used for that payment can tell it's your payment. Money you made private yourself can be traced back to the public account.

Anyone can tell that this pool was started by a payment from the Seedelf contract, and the private UTxOs used for that payment are tied to this pool's start. Whoever paid them to you can tell it's your payment. Money you made private yourself can be traced back to the public account. The change goes back to a new private UTxO.
A box that came back from this pool can't pay part of it without other money. At the current fees, that needs {{least}} ₳ per box.
A box that came back from this pool can't pay part of it without other money.
Some of the boxes were put in, addressed to your Seedelf key, by another person or another device. If you mix them, this mix and the private UTxOs used are tied to the person who put them in.
Another person or another device has put boxes in, addressed to your Seedelf key. "Remix boxes" doesn't handle them, and they don't come back automatically either.
Another person or another device has put {{count}} boxes in, addressed to your Seedelf key. "Remix boxes" doesn't handle them, and they don't come back automatically either.
Only boxes that came back from Lovejoin, and money other people paid you, can separate a Seedelf from the public account. Money you made private yourself can be traced back to the account.
This Seedelf is yours. The payment goes into the private balance.
Recipient {{number}}'s Seedelf is yours. That payment goes into the private balance.
That's a script address. This payment has no datum attached. With some scripts it becomes unusable forever; with others, anyone can withdraw it.
Recipient {{number}} is a script address. That payment has no datum attached. With some scripts it becomes unusable forever; with others, anyone can withdraw it.
Seedelf Wallet can't display the "{{character}}" in the tag. Please use half-width alphanumeric characters, spaces and symbols.
It isn't in the wallet's list. Anyone can imitate a known token's name, so check the ID before swapping.
It's in neither the wallet's list nor Minswap's verified list. Anyone can imitate a known token's name, so check the ID before swapping.
Above {{percent}}, someone trading just before the swap can bring the amount you receive down to near the minimum.
{{token}} isn't in the wallet's list, and Minswap hasn't verified its ID either. Anyone can imitate a known token's name, so check the ID before swapping.
Swap to this token anyway
Yours (Seedelf Wallet can't use it yet)
This DRep calls itself by the name of one of the wallet's own options. The voting rights go to this DRep, not to that option.

Unless you turn on site connections, it adds nothing to web pages. When you turn it on, it adds only the standard Cardano wallet entry (window.cardano) to https pages and to pages served from this device itself (localhost, 127.0.0.1). So, as with other Cardano wallets, any of those pages can recognize that you're using Seedelf Wallet. Before anything is signed, the wallet checks with you.

verdicts.why: Says the same: the file isn't encrypted, and its Made private and Made public rows (quoted with the app's own row labels, プライベートにしました / 公開しました) show those payments went into or came out of the private balance.
Keeps all three parts: it pays a Seedelf, the money comes from the public account, and it happens in the open (公然と).
Keeps all three parts: it pays a Seedelf, the money comes from this private session's one-time account (使い捨てアカウント, the house term), and it happens in the open.
Same meaning. 表示と makes 'differ' explicit as 'differ from what is shown', which is what the code means: the site can send other metadata, or none.
Same cause and effect: it pays under a register that is already on chain, so anyone can tell whose Seedelf it goes to.
Same: it pays a Seedelf with a reference script attached, and Seedelf Wallet can't spend it yet (まだ…使用できません, the house's word for spend).

Every clause is there: someone else or another device put these boxes in under your Seedelf key; mixing them from the private balance ties the mix to whoever did; and the quoted button, which matches lovejoin.payPrivateAnyway, takes them. The も ('too') does no harm, since that button does include them.

All three statements hold: anyone sees that a spend from the Seedelf contract started a pool, whoever paid you the money can tell it was yours, and money you made private yourself leads back to the public account. Rendering 'spend' as 支払い keeps the meaning.

Same: a box that comes back from this pool can't pay out part of itself without other money, and at current fees that takes {{least}} ₳ per box. The placeholder is kept.
Same as the English: a box that comes back from this pool can't pay out part of itself without other money.
Same: some of these boxes were put in under your Seedelf key by someone else or another device, and mixing them ties both this mix and the private UTxOs it spends (使うプライベート UTxO) to whoever did.

Same: someone else or another device put boxes in under your key, the quoted 「ボックスを再ミックス」 (matching lovejoin.again) leaves them out, and they never come back by themselves. With the count hidden, the bare ボックスを says 'some boxes' well enough.
Same, with the {{count}} placeholder kept in the glossary's ボックス…N 件 form. 'Mix my boxes again' leaves them out, and they never come back by themselves.

The 'only' survives (…だけです): only boxes back from Lovejoin and money others paid you keep the Seedelf apart from the public account, and self-made-private money leads back to it. The bare アカウント clearly points back to the 公開アカウント just named.
Same: this Seedelf is yours, and the payment goes into the private balance.
Same, with {{number}} kept and 宛先 used for 'recipient' as the glossary says.

Same: it's a script's address, the payment carries no datum, some scripts can never spend it (it becomes unusable forever), and some let anyone take it. The blind back-translation read the relative clause the right way.
Same as send.warn.script, with {{number}} kept and 宛先 used for 'recipient'.
Same: the wallet can't show 「{{character}}」 in a tag. 半角の英数字、スペース、記号 is the Japanese way to say plain letters, digits, spaces and punctuation, which is the code's printable-ASCII rule (0x20–0x7E).
Same: the token isn't on the wallet's list, anyone can copy a known token's name, so check the ID before swapping into it.
The 'neither…nor' is kept (…にも…にも含まれていません), and so are the copied-name warning and the ID check.
Same: above {{percent}}, someone trading just before your swap can leave the amount you receive near its minimum.
Same: {{token}} isn't on the wallet's list, Minswap hasn't verified its ID, anyone can copy a known token's name, so check the ID before you swap into it.
Same switch label: swap into this token anyway.
Same: yours, but Seedelf Wallet can't spend it yet. The parenthesis follows the other tx.yours.* labels.
Same: the DRep goes by the name of one of the wallet's own options, and the voting power (投票権, the house term) goes to this DRep, not to that option.

The Japanese lists the allowed characters as 半角の英数字と記号 ('half-width letters, digits and symbols') and leaves out spaces. A tag can hold any printable ASCII character, spaces included (labelProblem allows 0x20–0x7E), and the English 'plain characters' covers spaces. The sibling warning shared.label.warn.badCharacter lists スペース on its own, so in this wallet 記号 doesn't include spaces. A Japanese user is told spaces aren't allowed when they are.
verdicts.fix: 。半角の英数字、スペース、記号で最大 {{max}} 文字です（Seedelf Wallet が入力どおりに表示できるよう、アクセント付きの文字は不可）。

verdicts.why: Every clause holds: it adds nothing unless connecting sites is on (サイトの接続, the app's own word), then it adds only window.cardano to https and localhost pages, so those pages can tell you use Seedelf Wallet as with any Cardano wallet, and it asks before anything is signed.

again.english: . Up to {{max}} characters, in half-width alphanumerics, spaces and symbols (no accented characters, so that Seedelf Wallet can display it exactly as entered).

second.why: Each part matches the English ". Up to {{max}} plain characters, no accents, so Seedelf Wallet shows the tag as typed." The leading 。 joins on after the <code> prefix, as the English '. ' does. 最大 {{max}} 文字 is 'up to {{max}}'. 半角の英数字、スペース、記号 is the English's 'plain characters' made concrete, and it is the exact set the code allows: printable ASCII, U+0020 to U+007E (src/shared/label.ts). The English's own warning for the same rule spells it out the same way, as 'plain letters (no accents), digits, spaces and punctuation'. The corrected value also now uses the same wording as ja shared.label.warn.badCharacter, so it no longer leaves out the space. アクセント付きの文字は不可 is 'no accents', and Seedelf Wallet が入力どおりに表示できるよう is 'so Seedelf Wallet shows the tag as typed'. The tag is left unsaid, but the タグ field label and the line before it make it clear. The reason sits next to the character rule, as it does in the English. Seedelf Wallet stays in Latin letters, as the glossary requires, and {{max}} is kept.
